rachel_2386.name: Rachel
rachel_2386.who: Laban's younger daughter, Jacob's beloved wife, and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
key: Rachel met Jacob at a well while watering her father's sheep (Genesis 29).
Jacob served Laban seven years for her, but Laban first gave him Leah (Genesis 29).
After years of barrenness, God remembered Rachel and she bore Joseph (Genesis 30).
She secretly took her father's household gods when Jacob left Laban (Genesis 31).
She died giving birth to Benjamin and was buried on the way to Bethlehem (Genesis 35).

jesse_903.name: Jesse
jesse_903.who: A man of Bethlehem, grandson of Boaz and Ruth, and the father of King David.
key: Jesse is named as the son of Obed and grandson of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4).
Samuel anointed Jesse's youngest son David as the future king (1 Samuel 16).
Jesse sent David with food to his older brothers in Saul's army (1 Samuel 17).
David placed his parents under the protection of the king of Moab (1 Samuel 22).
Isaiah foretold a shoot from Jesse's stump, which Paul applies to Christ (Isaiah 11; Romans 15).

asher_337.name: Asher
asher_337.who: A son of Jacob by Zilpah, Leah's servant, and ancestor of the tribe of Asher.
key: Asher was born to Zilpah, and Leah named him, saying she was happy (Genesis 30).
He went down to Egypt with his sons and daughter Serah (Genesis 46).
Jacob blessed him, saying his food would be rich (Genesis 49).
Moses blessed Asher's tribe with abundance and strength (Deuteronomy 33).
His tribe received its inheritance along the northern coast (Joshua 19).

rehoboam_2412.name: Rehoboam
rehoboam_2412.who: Son of Solomon and first king of Judah after the kingdom divided.
key: Rehoboam went to Shechem to be made king over all Israel (1 Kings 12).
He rejected the elders' advice, and the northern tribes followed Jeroboam instead (1 Kings 12).
The prophet Shemaiah told him not to fight against Israel, and he obeyed (2 Chronicles 11).
After he forsook the Lord's law, Shishak of Egypt took the temple treasures (2 Chronicles 12).
He reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah succeeded him (1 Kings 14).

balak_387.name: Balak
balak_387.who: King of Moab, son of Zippor, who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
key: Fearing Israel, Balak sent for the prophet Balaam to curse them (Numbers 22).
Balaam blessed Israel instead each time Balak brought him to a new place (Numbers 23).
Balak sent Balaam away angry after a final prophecy of Israel's victory (Numbers 24).
Later Scripture recalls how God turned Balak's scheme into blessing (Joshua 24; Micah 6).
Jesus recalls Balaam teaching Balak to place a stumbling block before Israel (Revelation 2).

simeon_2741.name: Simeon
simeon_2741.who: Jacob's second son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Simeon.
key: Leah named him Simeon because the Lord heard she was unloved (Genesis 29).
With Levi, he killed the men of Shechem after Dinah was violated (Genesis 34).
Joseph kept Simeon bound in Egypt until the brothers returned with Benjamin (Genesis 42).
Jacob's final words condemned the violent anger of Simeon and Levi (Genesis 49).
His tribe received its inheritance within the territory of Judah (Joshua 19).

zadok_2973.name: Zadok
zadok_2973.who: A priest descended from Aaron who served King David and anointed Solomon king.
key: Zadok is listed with Ahimelech as a priest in David's government (2 Samuel 8).
During Absalom's revolt, David sent him back to Jerusalem with the ark (2 Samuel 15).
He anointed Solomon king at Gihon when Adonijah tried to seize the throne (1 Kings 1).
Solomon put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest (1 Kings 2).
Ezekiel's vision gives the sons of Zadok charge of the sanctuary (Ezekiel 44).

issachar_645.name: Issachar
issachar_645.who: Jacob's fifth son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Issachar.
key: Leah bore Issachar after giving Rachel her son's mandrakes (Genesis 30).
He went down to Egypt with his four sons (Genesis 46).
Jacob likened him to a strong donkey bending to labor (Genesis 49).
His tribe received land in the Jezreel region (Joshua 19).
Men of Issachar who understood the times joined David at Hebron (1 Chronicles 12).

merari_2004.name: Merari
merari_2004.who: The third son of Levi, whose descendants the Merarites served at the tabernacle.
key: Merari went down to Egypt with his father Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
The Merarites were assigned to carry the tabernacle frames, bars, and pillars (Numbers 3; Numbers 4).
His descendants received twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun (Joshua 21).
Merarite Levites, including the singer Ethan, served in David's temple music (1 Chronicles 6; 1 Chronicles 15).

midian_2075.name: Midian
midian_2075.who: A son of Abraham by Keturah and ancestor of the Midianites.
key: Keturah bore Midian and his brothers to Abraham (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to Keturah's sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).
Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah (1 Chronicles 1).
His descendants, the Midianites, later oppressed Israel until Gideon's victory (Judges 6).

samson_2468.name: Samson
samson_2468.who: A Nazirite from the tribe of Dan whom God empowered to judge Israel against the Philistines.
key: The angel of the Lord announced Samson's birth to Manoah's wife (Judges 13).
He married a Philistine woman of Timnah and posed a riddle at the feast (Judges 14).
He struck down a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone (Judges 15).
Delilah learned the secret of his strength, and the Philistines blinded him (Judges 16).
He pulled down the temple of Dagon, dying with the Philistines inside (Judges 16).

ahaz_118.name: Ahaz
ahaz_118.who: A king of Judah, son of Jotham, who turned to idols and to Assyria.
key: Ahaz did not do right and even burned his son as an offering (2 Kings 16).
When Syria and Israel attacked, Isaiah urged him to trust God and gave the Immanuel sign (Isaiah 7).
He sent temple silver and gold to Tiglath-pileser of Assyria for help (2 Kings 16).
He copied an altar from Damascus and later shut the temple doors (2 Chronicles 28).
His son Hezekiah succeeded him as king (2 Kings 16).

jehoiakim_1085.name: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim_1085.who: A son of Josiah whom Pharaoh Neco made king of Judah, and who opposed Jeremiah.
key: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim king and changed his name to Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23).
He taxed the land heavily to pay the tribute Egypt demanded (2 Kings 23).
He had the prophet Uriah brought back from Egypt and killed (Jeremiah 26).
He cut up and burned the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies (Jeremiah 36).
He served Nebuchadnezzar three years, then rebelled against him (2 Kings 24).

abimelech_41.name: Abimelech
abimelech_41.who: A son of Gideon by a concubine in Shechem, who made himself king by murder.
key: Abimelech was born to Gideon's concubine in Shechem (Judges 8).
He killed his seventy brothers on one stone, and Shechem made him king (Judges 9).
His surviving brother Jotham warned Shechem with a fable about the trees (Judges 9).
When Shechem turned against him, he destroyed the city (Judges 9).
At Thebez a woman dropped a millstone on him, and his armor-bearer killed him (Judges 9).

john_1677.name: John
john_1677.who: A fisherman, son of Zebedee and brother of James, who became one of Jesus' twelve apostles.
key: Jesus called John and James from mending nets with their father (Matthew 4; Mark 1).
Jesus named John and James Boanerges, meaning Sons of Thunder (Mark 3).
With Peter and James, he saw Jesus transfigured and was near him in Gethsemane (Mark 9; Mark 14).
With Peter, he was arrested after a lame man was healed in Jesus' name (Acts 3; Acts 4).
On the island of Patmos, he received the revelation of Jesus Christ (Revelation 1).

amaziah_214.name: Amaziah
amaziah_214.who: A king of Judah, son of Joash, who began well but turned to Edom's gods.
key: He executed his father's murderers but spared their children, as the Law commanded (2 Kings 14).
At a prophet's word, he sent home the Israelite soldiers he had hired (2 Chronicles 25).
He defeated Edom in the Valley of Salt, then worshiped Edom's gods (2 Chronicles 25).
He challenged Joash king of Israel and was defeated at Beth-shemesh (2 Kings 14).
Conspirators killed him at Lachish, and his son Uzziah became king (2 Kings 14).

lot_1830.name: Lot
lot_1830.who: Abraham's nephew, son of Haran, who settled near Sodom and was rescued from its destruction.
key: Lot traveled with his uncle Abram from Haran to Canaan (Genesis 12).
When their herds grew too large, Lot chose the Jordan valley near Sodom (Genesis 13).
Abram rescued Lot after invading kings captured him (Genesis 14).
Angels led Lot out of Sodom, and his wife became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19).
His daughters bore Moab and Ben-ammi, ancestors of Moab and Ammon (Genesis 19).

sihon_2739.name: Sihon
sihon_2739.who: King of the Amorites at Heshbon, defeated by Israel east of the Jordan.
key: Sihon refused Israel passage and attacked them, but Israel defeated him (Numbers 21).
Moses recalled that the Lord hardened Sihon's spirit and gave his land to Israel (Deuteronomy 2).
His territory was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad (Numbers 32).
Rahab and later generations remembered Sihon's defeat as the Lord's work (Joshua 2; Nehemiah 9).

uzziah_375.name: Uzziah
uzziah_375.who: A king of Judah, son of Amaziah, who reigned fifty-two years until pride brought leprosy.
key: Uzziah became king at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years (2 Chronicles 26).
As long as he sought the Lord, God made him prosper (2 Chronicles 26).
He won wars, built towers, and became famous for his strength (2 Chronicles 26).
He grew proud, burned incense in the temple, and was struck with leprosy (2 Chronicles 26).
Isaiah saw the Lord on his throne in the year Uzziah died (Isaiah 6).

asaph_330.name: Asaph
asaph_330.who: A Levite musician and seer appointed by David to lead worship before the ark.
key: David's Levites appointed Asaph to sound bronze cymbals in worship (1 Chronicles 15).
David put Asaph in charge of thanksgiving before the ark (1 Chronicles 16).
His sons prophesied with lyres, harps, and cymbals under his direction (1 Chronicles 25).
Hezekiah's Levites sang praise with the words of David and Asaph the seer (2 Chronicles 29).
Twelve psalms bear his name, including Psalms 50 and 73 through 83 (Psalms 73).

leah_1813.name: Leah
leah_1813.who: Laban's elder daughter, Jacob's first wife, and mother of six of his sons.
key: Laban gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel on the wedding night (Genesis 29).
The Lord saw she was unloved and gave her Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah (Genesis 29).
She later bore Issachar, Zebulun, and a daughter, Dinah (Genesis 30).
Jacob placed Leah and her children ahead of Rachel when meeting Esau (Genesis 33).
Jacob buried Leah in the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 49).

caleb_537.name: Caleb
caleb_537.who: Son of Jephunneh from Judah, one of the twelve spies, who wholly followed the Lord.
key: As one of twelve spies, Caleb urged Israel to go up and take the land (Numbers 13).
God promised that Caleb and Joshua alone of their generation would enter Canaan (Numbers 14).
At eighty-five, Caleb asked Joshua for Hebron as his inheritance (Joshua 14).
He drove out Anak's sons and gave his daughter Achsah to Othniel (Joshua 15).

eli_1072.name: Eli
eli_1072.who: The priest at Shiloh who judged Israel forty years and raised the young Samuel.
key: Eli mistook Hannah's silent prayer for drunkenness, then blessed her (1 Samuel 1).
A man of God announced judgment because Eli honored his wicked sons above God (1 Samuel 2).
Eli told the boy Samuel how to answer when the Lord called (1 Samuel 3).
Hearing that his sons were dead and the ark captured, he fell and died (1 Samuel 4).

nun_2214.name: Nun
nun_2214.who: An Ephraimite remembered as the father of Joshua.
key: Nun appears in the line of Ephraim as son of Elishama and father of Joshua (1 Chronicles 7).
Joshua is regularly called the son of Nun, from Moses' day onward (Exodus 33; Joshua 1).

abiathar_20.name: Abiathar
abiathar_20.who: A priest, son of Ahimelech, who escaped Saul's massacre and served David.
key: Abiathar alone escaped when Saul killed the priests of Nob, and fled to David (1 Samuel 22).
He brought the ephod, through which David inquired of the Lord (1 Samuel 30).
With Zadok he carried the ark during Absalom's revolt, then returned it (2 Samuel 15).
He supported Adonijah, so Solomon removed him from the priesthood (1 Kings 1; 1 Kings 2).
Jesus mentioned him when speaking of David eating the bread of the Presence (Mark 2).

ahasuerus_117.name: Ahasuerus
ahasuerus_117.who: The king of Persia who made Esther his queen.
key: Ahasuerus ruled 127 provinces and deposed Queen Vashti for refusing his summons (Esther 1).
He chose Esther as queen in Vashti's place (Esther 2).
He allowed Haman to issue a decree to destroy the Jews (Esther 3).
After a sleepless night, he had Mordecai honored for saving his life (Esther 6).
He had Haman hanged and allowed the Jews to defend themselves (Esther 7; Esther 8).

barnabas_1722.name: Barnabas
barnabas_1722.who: A Levite from Cyprus, called son of encouragement, who traveled with Paul as a missionary.
key: Joseph, called Barnabas by the apostles, sold a field and gave the money (Acts 4).
He brought the newly converted Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem (Acts 9).
Sent to Antioch, he brought Saul there to teach the church (Acts 11).
The Holy Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul for missionary work (Acts 13).
After the Jerusalem council, he parted from Paul over taking Mark (Acts 15).

kohath_1790.name: Kohath
kohath_1790.who: The second son of Levi and grandfather of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
key: Kohath went down to Egypt with Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
He lived 133 years, and his son Amram fathered Aaron and Moses (Exodus 6).
The Kohathites carried the most holy things of the tabernacle (Numbers 4).
Korah, who rebelled against Moses, was his grandson (Numbers 16).

nathan_2153.name: Nathan
nathan_2153.who: A prophet in David's court who delivered God's covenant promise and confronted David's sin.
key: Nathan told David that God would build him a lasting house and kingdom (2 Samuel 7).
He rebuked David's sin with Bathsheba through a parable about a lamb (2 Samuel 12).
He brought God's name for the infant Solomon, Jedidiah (2 Samuel 12).
He helped secure Solomon's succession and anointed him king (1 Kings 1).
He recorded events of David's and Solomon's reigns (1 Chronicles 29; 2 Chronicles 9).

rebekah_2401.name: Rebekah
rebekah_2401.who: Daughter of Bethuel, wife of Isaac, and mother of Esau and Jacob.
key: Abraham's servant found Rebekah at a well when she watered his camels (Genesis 24).
She agreed to go with him and became Isaac's wife (Genesis 24).
The Lord told her the older of her twins would serve the younger (Genesis 25).
She helped Jacob obtain Isaac's blessing in place of Esau (Genesis 27).
She sent Jacob to her brother Laban to escape Esau's anger (Genesis 27).

zerubbabel_3054.name: Zerubbabel
zerubbabel_3054.who: A descendant of David and governor of Judah who led exiles home and rebuilt the temple.
key: Zerubbabel led exiles from Babylon back to Jerusalem and Judah (Ezra 2).
With Jeshua he rebuilt the altar and laid the temple foundation (Ezra 3).
He refused the offer of the land's adversaries to help build (Ezra 4).
Urged by Haggai and Zechariah, he resumed work on the temple (Ezra 5; Haggai 1).
God called him a chosen signet ring (Haggai 2).

adam_78.name: Adam
adam_78.who: The first man, formed by God from dust and placed in the garden of Eden.
key: God formed Adam from the dust and placed him in Eden (Genesis 2).
God made the woman from Adam's rib and brought her to him (Genesis 2).
Adam ate the forbidden fruit and was sent out of the garden (Genesis 3).
He fathered Cain, Abel, and Seth, and lived 930 years (Genesis 4; Genesis 5).
Paul contrasts Adam, through whom death came, with Christ (Romans 5; 1 Corinthians 15).

ahaziah_121.name: Ahaziah
ahaziah_121.who: A king of Judah, son of Jehoram and Athaliah, who reigned one year.
key: Ahaziah became king at twenty-two and followed the ways of Ahab's house (2 Kings 8).
He joined Joram of Israel in war against Hazael at Ramoth-gilead (2 Kings 8).
Jehu's men wounded him while he fled, and he died at Megiddo (2 Kings 9).
After his death his sister Jehosheba hid his son Joash from Athaliah (2 Kings 11).

baasha_589.name: Baasha
baasha_589.who: A king of Israel from Issachar who seized the throne and destroyed Jeroboam's house.
key: Baasha killed King Nadab and struck down Jeroboam's whole house (1 Kings 15).
He fortified Ramah to cut off traffic to Asa king of Judah (1 Kings 15).
He withdrew when Asa paid Ben-hadad of Syria to attack him (2 Chronicles 16).
The prophet Jehu announced judgment on Baasha's house for his sins (1 Kings 16).
His son Elah reigned briefly before Zimri killed him (1 Kings 16).

gedaliah_1287.name: Gedaliah
gedaliah_1287.who: Son of Ahikam, appointed governor of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar after Jerusalem fell.
key: Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah governor over those left in Judah (2 Kings 25).
Jeremiah was entrusted to Gedaliah's care (Jeremiah 39; Jeremiah 40).
He urged the people to serve Babylon and live in the land (Jeremiah 40).
He disbelieved Johanan's warning about a plot against him (Jeremiah 40).
Ishmael son of Nethaniah murdered him at Mizpah (Jeremiah 41).

jehoiada_793.name: Jehoiada
jehoiada_793.who: The priest who protected the boy Joash and restored the line of David to Judah's throne.
key: He and his wife hid Joash in the temple for six years (2 Chronicles 22).
He crowned Joash king and had Athaliah put to death (2 Kings 11).
He led a covenant, and the people tore down the house of Baal (2 Kings 11).
He set up a chest to collect money for temple repairs (2 Kings 12).
He died at 130 and was buried among the kings (2 Chronicles 24).

jephthah_839.name: Jephthah
jephthah_839.who: A Gileadite warrior who judged Israel six years after defeating the Ammonites.
key: Driven out by his half-brothers, Jephthah was later recalled to lead Gilead (Judges 11).
He vowed an offering to the Lord and defeated the Ammonites (Judges 11).
His only daughter came out to meet him, and he kept his vow (Judges 11).
He defeated Ephraim, identifying them by the word Shibboleth (Judges 12).
Hebrews lists him among those who acted by faith (Hebrews 11).

korah_1795.name: Korah
korah_1795.who: A Levite, son of Izhar, who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron.
key: Korah was a grandson of Kohath, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
With Dathan, Abiram, and 250 leaders, he challenged Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).
The earth swallowed the rebels, and fire consumed the 250 men (Numbers 16).
Korah's sons did not die, and their descendants served in temple worship (Numbers 26).
Several psalms are titled for the sons of Korah (Psalms 42).

gershon_1305.name: Gershon
gershon_1305.who: The firstborn son of Levi, whose descendants the Gershonites served at the tabernacle.
key: Gershon went down to Egypt with Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
The Gershonites cared for the tabernacle's curtains, coverings, and screens (Numbers 3; Numbers 4).
His descendants received thirteen cities in Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh (Joshua 21).

nebat_2165.name: Nebat
nebat_2165.who: An Ephraimite of Zeredah, father of Jeroboam the first king of northern Israel.
key: Nebat is named as the Ephraimite father of Jeroboam, whose mother was Zeruah (1 Kings 11).
Later kings are compared to Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin (1 Kings 15; 2 Kings 17).

zeruiah_3055.name: Zeruiah
zeruiah_3055.who: David's sister and mother of his commanders Joab, Abishai, and Asahel.
key: Zeruiah and Abigail are listed as sisters of David and his brothers (1 Chronicles 2).
Her sons are usually named as the sons of Zeruiah (1 Samuel 26; 2 Samuel 2).
David said the sons of Zeruiah were too harsh for him (2 Samuel 3).

abishai_50.name: Abishai
abishai_50.who: A son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one of David's chief warriors.
key: Abishai went with David into Saul's camp and offered to kill Saul (1 Samuel 26).
With Joab he killed Abner to avenge their brother Asahel (2 Samuel 3).
He offered to kill Shimei for cursing David, but David refused (2 Samuel 16).
He commanded a third of David's army against Absalom (2 Samuel 18).
He rescued David by killing the giant Ishbi-benob (2 Samuel 21).

adonijah_97.name: Adonijah
adonijah_97.who: David's fourth son, born to Haggith, who tried to take the throne before Solomon.
key: Adonijah was born to David by Haggith at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
In David's old age, he declared himself king with Joab and Abiathar's support (1 Kings 1).
When Solomon was anointed, Adonijah fled to the altar and was spared (1 Kings 1).
He asked to marry Abishag, and Solomon had Benaiah put him to death (1 Kings 2).

boaz_519.name: Boaz
boaz_519.who: A worthy man of Bethlehem who redeemed and married Ruth, becoming David's great-grandfather.
key: Boaz, a relative of Elimelech, showed kindness to Ruth in his field (Ruth 2).
At the threshing floor, he promised to act as her redeemer (Ruth 3).
He redeemed Naomi's land at the city gate and married Ruth (Ruth 4).
Their son Obed became the grandfather of King David (Ruth 4).
Boaz appears in the genealogies of Jesus (Matthew 1; Luke 3).

jonah_1689.name: Jonah
jonah_1689.who: A prophet of Israel, son of Amittai, sent by God to preach to Nineveh.
key: Jonah foretold the restoration of Israel's borders under Jeroboam II (2 Kings 14).
Fleeing God's call, he was thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish (Jonah 1).
He prayed from inside the fish and was delivered onto dry land (Jonah 2).
He preached in Nineveh, and the city repented (Jonah 3).
Jesus pointed to the sign of Jonah as a picture of himself (Matthew 12).

manasseh_1930.name: Manasseh
manasseh_1930.who: A king of Judah, son of Hezekiah, whose long reign was marked by idolatry until he repented.
key: Manasseh became king at twelve and reigned fifty-five years (2 Kings 21).
He rebuilt high places, set idols in the temple, and burned his son (2 Kings 21).
He shed much innocent blood in Jerusalem (2 Kings 21).
Taken captive to Babylon, he humbled himself, and God restored him (2 Chronicles 33).
His sins are named as a cause of Judah's later judgment (2 Kings 24; Jeremiah 15).

timotheus_2863.name: Timothy
timotheus_2863.who: A young believer from Lystra who became Paul's trusted coworker and the recipient of two letters.
key: Paul took Timothy, son of a Jewish believer and a Greek father, on his travels (Acts 16).
Paul sent him to strengthen churches such as Thessalonica and Corinth (1 Thessalonians 3; 1 Corinthians 4).
He is named with Paul as co-sender of several letters (2 Corinthians 1; Philippians 1).
Paul left him at Ephesus to guard sound teaching (1 Timothy 1).
Hebrews mentions that Timothy had been released (Hebrews 13).

abimelech_40.name: Abimelech
abimelech_40.who: A Philistine king of Gerar who dealt with Abraham and with Isaac.
key: Abimelech took Sarah, but God warned him in a dream and he returned her (Genesis 20).
Abraham prayed, and God healed Abimelech's household (Genesis 20).
He made a covenant with Abraham at Beersheba over a well (Genesis 21).
Seeing Isaac with Rebekah, Abimelech rebuked him for calling her his sister (Genesis 26).
He later made a peace covenant with Isaac (Genesis 26).

benaiah_439.name: Benaiah
benaiah_439.who: Son of Jehoiada, a mighty warrior of David who became commander of Solomon's army.
key: Benaiah commanded David's bodyguard, the Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Samuel 8).
He killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day (2 Samuel 23).
He supported Solomon against Adonijah (1 Kings 1).
At Solomon's command he executed Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei (1 Kings 2).
Solomon made him commander of the army in Joab's place (1 Kings 2).

herod_1505.name: Herod Antipas
herod_1505.who: The tetrarch of Galilee who executed John the Baptist and questioned Jesus before his crucifixion.
key: Herod imprisoned John the Baptist for condemning his marriage to Herodias (Mark 6).
At his birthday feast, he had John beheaded (Matthew 14).
Hearing of Jesus, he wondered if John had risen from the dead (Luke 9).
Jesus called him that fox when warned that Herod wanted to kill him (Luke 13).
Pilate sent Jesus to Herod, who mocked him and sent him back (Luke 23).

hiram_1532.name: Hiram
hiram_1532.who: King of Tyre who supplied cedar and craftsmen for David's palace and Solomon's temple.
key: Hiram sent cedar, carpenters, and masons to build David's house (2 Samuel 5).
He agreed to supply Solomon with timber for the temple (1 Kings 5).
Solomon gave him twenty cities in Galilee, which displeased him (1 Kings 9).
His sailors brought gold from Ophir with Solomon's fleet (1 Kings 10).

joash_1633.name: Joash
joash_1633.who: A king of Israel, son of Jehoahaz and father of Jeroboam II.
key: Joash became king of Israel in Samaria and did evil (2 Kings 13).
He wept over the dying Elisha and struck the ground with arrows (2 Kings 13).
He defeated Ben-hadad three times and recovered Israel's cities (2 Kings 13).
He defeated Amaziah of Judah and broke down Jerusalem's wall (2 Kings 14).

judas_1760.name: Judas Iscariot
judas_1760.who: One of the twelve apostles, son of Simon Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.
key: Jesus chose Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve apostles (Matthew 10; Luke 6).
He kept the disciples' moneybag and stole from it (John 12).
He agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26).
He led the crowd to Jesus and identified him with a kiss (Mark 14).
Filled with remorse, he hanged himself, and Matthias replaced him (Matthew 27; Acts 1).

shaphan_2550.name: Shaphan
shaphan_2550.who: Secretary to King Josiah who read the newly found Book of the Law to the king.
key: Josiah sent Shaphan to the temple to arrange payment for repairs (2 Kings 22).
Hilkiah gave Shaphan the Book of the Law, and he read it to Josiah (2 Kings 22).
Josiah sent him with others to inquire of the prophetess Huldah (2 Kings 22).
His sons Ahikam and Gemariah later supported Jeremiah (Jeremiah 26; Jeremiah 36).

amalek_197.name: Amalek
amalek_197.who: A grandson of Esau, son of Eliphaz by Timna, and ancestor of the Amalekites.
key: Timna bore Amalek to Eliphaz, Esau's son (Genesis 36).
He is listed among the chiefs descended from Esau in Edom (Genesis 36).
His descendants, the Amalekites, attacked Israel at Rephidim (Exodus 17).
Saul was commanded to destroy the Amalekites but disobeyed (1 Samuel 15).

ezra_1245.name: Ezra
ezra_1245.who: A priest and scribe skilled in the Law of Moses who led exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem.
key: With King Artaxerxes' letter, Ezra led a group from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 7).
Grieved over intermarriage with the peoples, he prayed and led the people to repent (Ezra 9; Ezra 10).
He read the Book of the Law aloud to the assembled people (Nehemiah 8).
He led a procession at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 12).

og_2238.name: Og
og_2238.who: The Amorite king of Bashan, the last of the Rephaim, defeated by Israel.
key: Og came out against Israel at Edrei, and Israel defeated him (Numbers 21).
His iron bed was nine cubits long, showing his great size (Deuteronomy 3).
His kingdom was given to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Numbers 32).
His defeat is remembered in Israel's praise of God's love (Psalms 136).

uriah_2898.name: Uriah
uriah_2898.who: A Hittite soldier among David's mighty men, husband of Bathsheba.
key: While Uriah was at war, David took his wife Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11).
Uriah refused to go home while the ark and army were in tents (2 Samuel 11).
David had him placed at the front of the battle, where he died (2 Samuel 11).
Nathan confronted David for striking down Uriah and taking his wife (2 Samuel 12).
He is listed among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).

amnon_232.name: Amnon
amnon_232.who: David's firstborn son, by Ahinoam, who was killed by Absalom.
key: Amnon was born to David by Ahinoam at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
He violated his half-sister Tamar and then hated her (2 Samuel 13).
Two years later Absalom had him killed at a sheep-shearing feast (2 Samuel 13).

baruch_410.name: Baruch
baruch_410.who: Son of Neriah, the scribe and faithful companion of the prophet Jeremiah.
key: Baruch received the deed of the field Jeremiah bought at Anathoth (Jeremiah 32).
He wrote Jeremiah's words on a scroll and read them in the temple (Jeremiah 36).
After King Jehoiakim burned the scroll, he wrote it again (Jeremiah 36).
He was taken to Egypt with Jeremiah against their will (Jeremiah 43).
The Lord promised Baruch his life wherever he went (Jeremiah 45).

hazael_1463.name: Hazael
hazael_1463.who: An official who became king of Syria and repeatedly oppressed Israel.
key: God told Elijah to anoint Hazael king over Syria (1 Kings 19).
Elisha wept as he foretold the harm Hazael would do to Israel (2 Kings 8).
Hazael smothered King Ben-hadad and took the throne (2 Kings 8).
He seized Israel's land east of the Jordan (2 Kings 10).
He took Gath, and Joash of Judah paid him to spare Jerusalem (2 Kings 12).

ishmael_631.name: Ishmael
ishmael_631.who: Son of Nethaniah, of the royal family of Judah, who murdered the governor Gedaliah.
key: Johanan warned Gedaliah that the Ammonite king had sent Ishmael to kill him (Jeremiah 40).
Ishmael killed Gedaliah and others at Mizpah (Jeremiah 41).
He killed seventy of eighty pilgrims bringing offerings (Jeremiah 41).
When Johanan rescued his captives, Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites (Jeremiah 41).
